reference_title: A peptide-based human T cell leukemia virus type I vaccine containing T and B cell epitopes that induces high titers of neutralizing antibodies.
staged_human_resolution: Primary-publication review resolves this HTLV-I gp46 peptide set as generic HTLV-I infection/vaccine antigen rather than a malignancy-specific ATL tumour target. The study develops a peptide-based HTLV-I vaccine and demonstrates peptide-responsive lymphocytes across several HTLV-I-infected clinical groups, including HTLV-I-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis, adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, and healthy HTLV-I carriers. Under this atlas's viral-antigen rule, oncogenic-virus peptides are retained as cancer targets only when the peptide is investigated in a malignancy-specific tumour-antigen context.
staged_review_note: Human literature review of PMID 7527817 supports exclude/non_cancer_antigen at epitope-role level. Although ATL patients were among the tested subjects and the reference therefore contains a genuine cancer context, the gp46 peptide-vaccine programme was designed as a general HTLV-I vaccine and the same helper epitope was studied across ATL, HAM/TSP, and healthy HTLV-I carriers. This is therefore generic viral infection/vaccine antigen evidence rather than malignancy-specific ATL target evidence. Reference-level cancer context and epitope-level cancer-target relevance must remain separate.

staged_review_note: Post-validation adjudication v1. PMID 15837732; epitope http://www.iedb.org/epitope/1872156; exact sequence GVLQGITSWGSEPCALPERP. Primary source: 15837732.pdf; PDF pages 1-4;6-8; Figure 1B; Figure 4; Figures 5-7; Figure 8B-C; Methods and minimal-epitope Results; SHA-256 de1d6901c84257f0ed29506776b799ac6afbad572993dc6724e0c7ce084649d2. exact_sequence_verification: Verified visually in Figure 1B: the printed PSA sequence and explicitly bracketed 221-240 reagent give GVLQGITSWGSEPCALPERP across the line wrap. | experiment_attribution: Exact PSA221-240 20-mer used to establish human CD4 lines; Figure 4 tests peptide presentation by DRB1*1501-expressing versus parental BLC. Figure 8B-C tests the CD4 line tested in Figure 8 with original 20-mer and shorter 13-mer separately. | biological_role_evidence: PSA target epitope investigated for prostate-cancer immunotherapy; includes granulomatous-prostatitis donors and one prostate-cancer patient, rather than a therapeutic efficacy trial. | exact_cd4_mhc2_evidence: Human peptide-specific lines were CD4-positive/CD8-negative; direct IFNg ELISA and thymidine proliferation. Figure 8 tests a prostate-cancer-derived CD4 line. | hla_restriction_evidence: DRB1*15:01 presentation is experimentally supported by engineered BLC-DR2b comparison (Figure 4); HLA-DR blocking in Figure 5 supports class specificity. Some parental BLC reactivity occurs in three donors; restriction is not universally exclusive. | native_processing_and_interpretation_limits: DC presentation of purified PSA and PSA-transfected HEK293 lysate supports processing recognized by 20-mer-specific lines. It does not demonstrate direct prostate-tumour recognition or tumour killing, or naturally displayed intact 20-mer length. | iedb_discrepancy_or_limit: IEDB assay 18141051 is Positive and cites Figure 4/Figure 8B-C, consistent with the 20-mer evidence. Protein/lysate experiments remain separate from exact-peptide assays. | Scientific review note: Approved for include/cancer_target. The original publication identifies the exact PSA221–240 sequence (GVLQGITSWGSEPCALPERP) in Figure 1B and demonstrates peptide-specific human CD4 T-cell responses in Figures 4 and 8. The peptide was investigated as a prostate-cancer immunotherapy target. Protein/lysate recognition represents separate experimental evidence; direct prostate-tumour recognition and clinical vaccine efficacy are not established. | Biological target role is independent of response polarity and does not imply immunogenicity, clinical efficacy or native tumour recognition. staged_human_resolution: include_as_cancer_target
staged_review_note: PMID 22159452; exact exported peptide GNWQYFFPVIFSKAS. MAGE-A3 141–155 tumour-antigen-specific CD4 SKIL response after full-antigen TriMix-DC vaccination. Assay pattern: positive in designated CD4 SKIL cytokine assay; CD8 blood/SKIL Table2 columns negative (separate subset). Attribution: B: exact 15-mer-pulsed EBV-B APC plus separately linked full-MAGE-A3 construct response. Priming: Full-length MAGE-A3 mRNA DC vaccine with class-II targeting signal; DTH vaccine/DC exposure; IL2 culture and pool then individual-peptide deconvolution. Epitope != immunogen is intentional. MHC-II: CD4 functional cytokine evidence (Th1; Fig4); generic class-II interpretation. Known DR4/DR7 overlap annotation does not establish restriction in this DR1/DR13 patient. Endogenous/tumour limit: Exact peptide plus full-antigen construct processing linked; clinical tumour response reference-context only; no direct tumour-cell recognition for this exact pair. Do not assign B52 from the nested known class-I annotation or DR4/DR7 from cited overlap to this CD4 experiment. HIV-Nef is a separate explicit control. Source: Original Methods; Table2 image MAGE-A3 141–155; Fig4c and Results.

staged_human_resolution: include_as_cancer_target
staged_review_note: Post-validation adjudication v1. PMID 22529020; epitope http://www.iedb.org/epitope/1350619; exact sequence CPLERFAELVGPVIP. Primary source: 22529020.pdf; PDF pages 2-3;6-9; Methods: Peptide immunization; Figures 3-5 (mouse); Figure 6A-B (human); Discussion; SHA-256 79998eec3edcb07f84a68476415ba5feae72fea2e990b9ff12f79d7fe3c59138. exact_sequence_verification: Verified in Methods PDF3: CPLERFAELVGPVIP is PAP351-365. | experiment_attribution: Exact 15-mer is a PAP epitope-mapping target candidate. Human enriched CD4 cultures were stimulated twice and tested by IFNg ELISA (Figure6A); mouse vaccine/mapping/processing studies are distinct. | biological_role_evidence: PAP prostate-cancer target candidate evaluated after PAP DNA vaccination; not a control or excluded solely because human response is negative. | exact_cd4_mhc2_evidence: Direct human enriched-CD4 negative functional result; positive mouse results cannot supply positive human CD4 evidence. | hla_restriction_evidence: DR1 transgenic-mouse and anti-DR inhibition support mouse HLA-DR context. Human subjects are DRB1*01:01 typed but negative PAP351-365 response cannot experimentally establish human restriction. Figure6B anti-DR blocking concerns PAP191-205. | native_processing_and_interpretation_limits: Mouse native-PAP recognition supports murine processing; no demonstrated human exact-peptide native recognition or clinical efficacy. | iedb_discrepancy_or_limit: IEDB 13690571 Negative/Fig6A agrees. Publication has internal coordinate inconsistency: abstract/introduction mention PAP181-195 human response, whereas human Results, Figure6 and Discussion identify PAP191-205. Neither positive claim belongs to PAP351-365. | Scientific review note: Approved for include/cancer_target. The Methods explicitly identify CPLERFAELVGPVIP as PAP351–365, a prostate-cancer-associated PAP epitope evaluated in target-mapping studies. Positive responses in HLA-DR1 transgenic mice support its experimental target role, whereas human enriched-CD4 cultures did not show a significant response to this peptide in Figure 6A. The human negative result and mouse positive findings must remain separate. Cancer-target classification does not imply demonstrated human immunogenicity or experimentally confirmed human allele-specific restriction for this peptide. | Biological target role is independent of response polarity and does not imply immunogenicity, clinical efficacy or native tumour recognition. Original IEDB measurements remain unchanged.

reference_title: Personalized peptide vaccine-induced immune response associated with long-term survival of a metastatic cholangiocarcinoma patient.
staged_human_resolution:
Primary-publication review resolves the current peptide as a
non-mutated tumour-associated vaccine target in the personalized
cholangiocarcinoma immunotherapy study. Although tumour-specific
mutated epitopes were predicted from sequencing, they could not be
validated as naturally presented HLA ligands by mass spectrometry.
The investigators therefore pursued vaccination using non-mutated
tumour-associated HLA ligands/peptides. The current peptide belongs to
that cancer-vaccine target set.
staged_review_note:
Human literature review of PMID 27397612 supports
include/cancer_target. These peptides are non-mutated
tumour-associated vaccine targets rather than WT comparators to a
mutant peptide. Non-mutated self origin does not automatically imply
relevant_comparator when the peptide itself is the intended TUMAP
target. Assay positivity or response magnitude does not determine
target identity.

reference_title: Targeting B-cell malignancies through human B-cell receptor specific CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells.
staged_human_resolution: Primary-publication review resolves these B-cell-receptor-derived peptides as tumour idiotype/BCR targets in B-cell malignancies. The study explicitly treats the BCR expressed by the clonal B-cell tumour as a tumour-specific idiotype antigen and identifies BCR-derived CD4 T-cell epitopes capable of recognition of autologous primary tumour.
staged_review_note: Human literature review of PMID 27999743 supports include/cancer_target. These peptides are deliberately studied as BCR/idiotype tumour-antigen targets in B-cell malignancy. Some epitopes are shared across multiple tumours and T cells could also be expanded from normal donors, but those observations do not convert the peptide's study-specific tumour-target role into a comparator role.

staged_review_note: PMID 36427494; exact exported peptide GDFGLATVKSRWSGS. BRAF-WT593–607 investigated as antitumour antigen alongside V600E in papillary-thyroid-cancer PBMCs. Assay pattern: mixed modalities: positive/low class-II tetramer detection and increased counts after stimulation; no increased IFNg reported. Attribution: A: exact WT15-mer tetramer/peptide assay. Priming: Patient PBMCs, then overnight exact WT peptide plus IL2/IL7/IL15; previous in-vivo priming unspecified. MHC-II: CD4 class-II tetramer/nonfunctional evidence; stimulated count increase; no secure allele-specific functional MHC-II proof. DQ8 reagent/cited context retained without upgrading. Endogenous/tumour limit: PTC reference-context only; no exact-pair tumour recognition. Tumour tetramer staining attempted but no BRAF-specific cells detected (data not shown). Eligible as secondary tetramer class-II evidence, not primary functional evidence. Ki67 mentioned in Methods does not establish a reported exact-pair proliferation result. DQ8-positive/negative participants and inconsistent counts are provenance/interpretation warnings. Separate HIV control; WT role is an independently studied target, not inferred comparator. Source: Original pp854 Methods; pp856 class-II Results; pp857 Fig3 legend.

Functional T-cell response positivity does not determine biological role.
